summary:
A poetic tribute to NASA’s discarded and retired equipment across the Moon, Mars and deep space. Although some missions have ended and their equipment remains on distant worlds, their contributions have not disappeared. Their observations, experiments and discoveries have helped scientists understand other planets, explore unfamiliar environments and develop knowledge that continues to benefit humanity. This poem aims to introduce younger audiences to the lesser-known side of space exploration: what happens to the technology after its mission is complete?. I hope to inspire curiosity, appreciation and a deeper understanding of NASA’s exploration history. 

A mission may end, but its legacy continues. Abandoned does not mean forgotten.
